intended_object: The canonical natural isomorphism, as functors of commutative k-algebras A, between the pointwise quotient presheaf A ↦ SLₙ(A)/Z(SLₙ)(A) (by the scheme-theoretic center) and the presheaf A ↦ PSLₙ(A) = SLₙ(A)/Z(SLₙ(A)). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation (Milne, Algebraic Groups, Ex. 5.49/21.4).
explanation:
The definition builds its components from `centerPointwiseQuotientIsoPSL`. That is `QuotientGroup.congr` along the standard equivalence `pointsMulEquiv` between SLₙ-points and determinant-one matrices. It uses the fact, proved just before, that this equivalence carries the represented center onto `Subgroup.center (SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) A)`. These components are conjugated by `eqToIso` so that the objects line up with `pointwiseQuotientFunctor` and `pslPointsFunctor`. Naturality comes from `centerPointwiseQuotientIsoPSL_hom_naturality`, which checks that the class of a point is sent to the class of its matrix and that this commutes with extension of scalars (`projectiveMap`). So this is the canonical identification of SLₙ/μₙ (pointwise, before sheafification) with PSLₙ, natural in A, as the docstring says.

The base k is a field because the library's center construction (`centerDefiningIdeal`) is only set up over a field, so the definition does need that setting. The hypothesis `0 < n` is needed for the identification of the center with roots of unity that the proof uses. The case n = 0 is trivial, so leaving it out is not a real loss of generality. Mathlib has no such natural isomorphism, since it has no center group scheme or pointwise Hopf-quotient presheaf.
